Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(n=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). We work modulo \(p\).

For \(n<k<p\), the interval \((k,2k]\) contains \(p\), while \(k!\) does not contain a factor of \(p\). Hence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\]

So the sum only needs \(0\le k\le n\).

For \(0\le k\le n\), since \(n\equiv -\frac12 \pmod p\),

\[
\binom{n}{k}(-4)^k
\equiv
\frac{(-\frac12)(-\frac32)\cdots(-\frac{2k-1}{2})}{k!}(-4)^k
=
\frac{2^k(1\cdot3\cdots(2k-1))}{k!}
=
\binom{2k}{k}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k \equiv \binom{n}{k}(-8)^k \pmod p.
\]

Thus

\[
S \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{n} k\binom{n}{k}(-8)^k.
\]

Using

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{n} k\binom{n}{k}x^k = xn(1+x)^{n-1},
\]

with \(x=-8\),

\[
S \equiv -8n(1-8)^{n-1}
= -8\cdot1013\cdot(-7)^{1012}.
\]

Since \(-8\cdot1013=-4(p-1)\equiv 4\pmod p\),

\[
S \equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,

\[
7^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)\pmod{2027}.
\]

Using quadratic reciprocity,

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=
-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=
-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
=
-1.
\]

So \(7^{1013}\equiv -1\), hence \(7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\). Therefore

\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since \(2027=7\cdot289+4\), we have \(7\cdot289\equiv -4\pmod{2027}\), so

\[
-4\cdot7^{-1}\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
